deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is a draft announcement of a lecture course, written twice: first in Latin for the official university Index Lectionum, then in German for the German-language course list.

Latin: 'Theoriam aequationum differentialia partialia continentium exponet et ad varias quaestiones physicas applicabit quinis p[er] hebd[omadem] scholis h[ora] X.' This means: '[Riemann] will expound the theory of equations containing partial differentials and apply it to various physical questions, in five lectures per week at 10 o'clock.'

German: 'Theorie der partiellen Differentialgleichungen mit Anwendung auf physikalische Probleme, fünfmal wöchentlich 10–11 Uhr.' Riemann first wrote 'Fragen' ('questions'), struck it out and replaced it with 'Probleme' ('problems'). The German therefore departs slightly from the Latin 'quaestiones'. It also differs from the later published title, which uses 'Fragen'.

Context: the next page is a notice signed 'Göttingen, den 30. April 1860, B. Riemann (Sternwarte)' about a lecture on gravitation, electricity and magnetism. This makes it likely that the present draft belongs to the Göttingen course announcements of about 1860. Riemann gave a course of this title several times, starting in winter 1854/55. Hattendorff's posthumous edition, 'Partielle Differentialgleichungen und deren Anwendung auf physikalische Fragen' (1869), is based on these lectures. No derivation is present to reconstruct.

results.what: Announcement of a five-hour-per-week lecture course on the theory of partial differential equations with physical applications (Latin and German versions).
results.modern_name: Lecture course on mathematical physics / PDEs (the basis of Riemann–Hattendorff 'Partielle Differentialgleichungen und deren Anwendung auf physikalische Fragen', 1869)
results.usually_credited_to: Bernhard Riemann (lectures, edited by K. Hattendorff)

deep.surprise_reason: This is an administrative lecture announcement with no mathematical content. Riemann's PDE lecture course is well documented and was published posthumously by Hattendorff. The only minor detail is the self-correction from 'Fragen' to 'Probleme'.
transcription_corrections: Latin abbreviations should be expanded: 'p. hebd.' = 'per hebdomadem', 'h. X' = 'hora X' (10 o'clock).

German line: the deletion at the end of line 1 appears to be 'Fragen' (written as 'Frag-'), with 'Probleme' inserted above the line. The struck-through word at the start of line 2 also appears to be 'Probleme' (or the continuation of the first wording). The final reading is 'mit Anwendung auf physikalische Probleme'.
'49' is the archival folio number, not part of Riemann's text.
